FIGURE 2 From lattice science to the design of Li–S battery separators. This timeline delineates the evolution of lattice engineering from fundamental solid-state physics to functional separator design. We bridge classical crystallography (Bragg, Bloch) with emerging nano-lattice strategies, highlighting a paradigm shift from passive physical barriers to dynamic catalytic membranes. Key advances include defect-rich 2D frameworks (MXene/MOF) and single-atom catalysts (SACs) that leverage lattice strain and coordination environments to achieve selective ion sieving and accelerate redox kinetics, thereby suppressing the shuttle effect at its origin.

FIGURE 17 Schematic illustration of the multidimensional synergy in “Lattice Leap” engineering for LSBs. This figure encapsulates the transformative journey from atomic-scale lattice manipulation (encompassing defects, strain, and interfacial dynamics) to macroscopic battery performance. By effectively mitigating intrinsic electrochemical challenges, notably the polysulfide shuttle and Li dendrite growth, this strategy unlocks high-energy-density storage ( > 450 Wh kg− 1 ) with exceptional stability. Crucially, preserving these functions throughout prolonged cycling—against both the structural evolution of the coating itself and the continuously evolving, polysulfide-containing electrolyte—remains a critical open challenge, and addressing it is a prerequisite for practical LSBs in demanding energy-storage applications.
